title: Close with thanks
line: Seven evenings ending the day in gratitude.
intro: Athena ends every lesson with gratitude. Εὐχαριστία, thanksgiving, from εὖ (good) and χάρις (grace), activates grace, the factor no one can calculate, which together with your own effort completes eudaimonia: as the old proverb says, with Athena (the goddess), move your hand too. For seven evenings you close the day the same way.
does: Each evening for a week, three thanks, and one thing that came to you unasked.
trains: Gratitude, and openness to grace alongside your own effort.
each: Before you sleep, name three things from today you are grateful for, however small, and say thank you for them. Then name one effort of yours from the day, and one thing that came to you without your doing: your hand moving, and the grace that met it.
note: Your three thanks today, and one thing that came to you unasked.
end: After seven evenings, where did you see your effort and grace working together? Has anything changed in how your days end?
